name: Muse Code

surfaces.label: Muse Code in a terminal (muse, muse exec, muse resume); launcher install execs muse-bin-<version>, Homebrew cask runs muse-aarch64-macos or muse-x86-macos as `muse`
muse serve: Muse Session Protocol host over stdio, spawned by @muse-code/sdk, ACP adapters and third-party GUIs; one process can hold several sessions

working_signals.meaning: raise only. session.jsonl is append-only and gets a line per run, model and tool event, but a long model call or tool call can leave it quiet. Maps only when the process was started with --session-id; a fresh or resumed TUI session has no id in argv. --no-session-log writes nothing.

inferred: agent shell commands run in a Seatbelt sandbox on macOS, so a shell (or a sandbox-exec wrapper, which this signal would miss) sits as a direct child only while a tool runs. Blind while the model streams. Not seen on a live process.
fallback guess, never measured; a turn waiting on the network burns almost none

waiting_signals.meaning: documented: fires when the agent needs your approval
documented event name; fires on an approval request. Exact timing relative to Notification is not documented
documented in the changelog: muse serve clients receive live session status changes and an attention flag when a session has a pending approval or input. Needs a client attached to the serve process

third-party (ccmux rules, captured from Muse Code 1.0.3): trust prompt text 'Do you trust this workspace?'; input frame '⟩' with no '◇ Thinking' line means idle at the composer. The composer frame stays visible while working. Not readable by a command-line matcher

hooks.config: hooks block in ~/.config/muse/settings.json (schema_version must be 1); project <project-root>/.muse/hooks.json after workspace trust; managed file named by managed_hooks_path. Shape: {"hooks": {"<Event>": [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "..."}]}]}}. Payload arrives as JSON on stdin with hook_event_name, session_id, turn_id, model (stdin and field names are from the SigNoz script only; dev.meta.ai does not describe the payload). SigNoz says a project .muse/hooks.json is silently ignored while dev.meta.ai says it loads after trust: unresolved, so prefer the settings.json block. Hooks run through your shell outside the sandbox with a cleared environment plus a small allowlist (official).

telemetry.how: No documented native OpenTelemetry switch found on dev.meta.ai. SigNoz says Muse Code 'ships its own OpenTelemetry exporter' but gives no setting and uses a hook script instead: UserPromptSubmit to Stop with turn_id brackets a turn, and PostLLMCall carries the W3C meta.traceparent that Muse attaches to every model call. Product telemetry is disabled with TBH_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 (seen in SDK QA source). MUSE_TRANSPORT_TRACE=1 prints provider lines to stderr.

sources.claim: Muse Code is Meta's coding agent for the terminal and CI; interactive TUI (muse), headless (muse exec), and muse serve / muse schema for the session protocol; install puts a native muse binary on the path; no desktop app or bundle id is documented

sources.claim: session.jsonl holds one JSON record per line with keys schema_version, id, stream{kind,id}, sequence, recorded_at (microseconds), record_type, durability, causation_id, payload_type, payload_schema_version, payload; run events use payload_type runtime.session, payload.kind run, event.kind started / model_completed / assistant_message_committed. The event that closes a run is not in any source I could read; the first line of the fixture is instead a retained-frame wrapper with keys retained_frame, frame_schema_version, children (child_index, record_json), which the parser also handles, so a reader must not assume every line has the record keys
sources.evidence: keys of every line of the synthetic fixture https://github.com/skzv/ccmux internal/muse/testdata/native-session.jsonl (8 lines, checked locally: line 1 is the frame wrapper, lines 2-8 the record shape); parser internal/muse/log.go (fixture is synthetic, so real files are unverified)

notes: Never seen running. The process name depends on the install: the launcher (install.sh) execs ~/.local/bin/muse-bin-<version> with that full path as argv[0], so the name changes with every release and only the path fragment /muse-bin- is stable; the Homebrew cask runs as plain `muse`. The bare name `muse` is short and could collide with another program, and matching cannot tell: prefer an open .session.lock under the sessions tree (lsof) as a second check. The launcher itself is a bash script (argv[0] bash) that execs, plus a detached bash subshell for background updates: neither matches. exclude_args is an exact match on any word, so a session literally named like a listed subcommand is hidden. The daemon surface also vetoes exec and resume, so `muse exec "explain serve"` stays the TUI surface; a bare `muse serve` still reaches the daemon. A prompt that is a separate argv word equal to serve would still be labelled daemon. exclude_args entries -h, -V, --help, --version and plugins are not documented on dev.meta.ai (plugins is only a slash command there); they are inert guesses. /muse-bin- is a substring of argv[0], so an unrelated directory named muse-bin-something would match; the versioned launcher form is the only one seen. muse exec is a one-shot: alive means working. The most precise turn signal is a hook pair UserPromptSubmit (turn_id) to Stop, or Interrupt on Esc; it needs settings.json edited. Without hooks there is no exact open-turn signal in the store that I could confirm, so transcript writes may only raise working. A goal set with /goal makes Muse queue follow-up turns after Stop, and four background observer agents make their own model calls, so activity can continue between visible turns. A trusted-workspace prompt and approval prompts block the turn while the process stays alive and quiet.
